plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Exit SMH due to being below its stop and de-risk the portfolio.
Trim QQQI to 20% and CRWD to 5% to reduce concentration and meet mandate limits.
Increase SPY to 15% to favor broad index exposure.
This plan aims for capital preservation and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdown. Expect modest returns with reduced risk.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%, and MUU to 2% to reduce overall leverage.
Reduce QQQI to 25% to meet concentration limits.
Trim SMH to 5% due to being below its stop.
Buy ZS at 5% and XLF at 5% as high-scoring scanner setups.
This plan balances risk and growth with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It blends broad index exposure with quality tech and a small amount of leverage. Expect moderate returns with controlled drawdown.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% and SMH to 5% to meet mandate limits and manage risk.
Add to SOXL, SPAL, and MUU to 6% each, leaning into leveraged ETFs.
Buy ZS at 10% and XLF at 10%, concentrating in high-scoring scanner setups.
This plan aims for stretch growth with a smaller cash buffer.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs decay daily.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Exit SMH due to being below its stop and CRWD to cut high-beta names.
Increase QQQI to 30% and SPY to 30% for steady monthly distributions.

income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index funds. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are variable.
